steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
To make the chocolate filling: Whisk 2 cups sugar, cocoa, and flour together in a saucepan. Blend in evaporated milk and vanilla.
Beat egg yolks and stir into chocolate filling.
Add butter and heat, stirring constantly, until butter is just melted.
Pour filling into unbaked pie shell.
Bake in the preheated oven until pie is just set, about 35 to 40 minutes.
To make the meringue topping: Beat egg whites in a glass, metal, or ceramic bowl until foamy. Gradually add sugar, continuing to beat until stiff peaks form.
Spread meringue over pie filling, covering completely.
Return pie to oven and bake until meringue is lightly browned and golden, about 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Bev's Chocolate Pie
raw_recipe.description: This chocolate pie has a luscious filling made with cocoa, sugar, egg yolks, and evaporated milk baked in a pie shell with fluffy meringue on top.

review.reviewBody:
WOW! We are picky! Hubby and I just got back from vacation and he loved the chocolate pie at dinner one evening. I tried some recipes and they turned out with a brownie texture, tried others and they were basically perked up pudding...But this recipe was IT! (Even better than the restaurant's!!! 
I made a homemade crust, doubled the vanilla and instead of a 12 ounce can of evap milk, I used 10 ounces. --(2) 5 ounce cans, used granulated sugar which quickly dissolved. Not runny or grainy or lumpy. 170 pound hubby ate 1 1/4 pies in 24 hour time span! LOL

Thanks for the wonderful recipe! I made a few changes - had no evaporated milk so substituted 8oz whole milk and 4 oz half and half. Added a dash of salt to dry ingredients, lowered sugar to 1.5 c, mixed beaten yolks with milks for easier adding. Stirred continuously during the heating process, and waited to add the butter till the mixture had heated up just a bit so stirring in would be easier. I’d also recommend adding the butter in pieces. Added vanilla to chocolate after removing from heat. Pie set right at 45 minutes, as recipe states. For the meringue, added dash of salt at beginning of mixing, added sugar by the tablespoon slowly during process, also added 1/2 tsp of vanilla. Add the meringue onto the hot pie immediately after pulling from the oven or you risk the meringue weeping. When removing from oven after meringue has set, leave out about an hour before placing in the fridge to cool completely.
 The end result was beautiful and delicious! I’ve seen some reviews stating the pie had no flavor. The added salt and vanilla helped, but the pie is VERY chocolatey so I’m unsure why anyone would say tasteless. As far as any issue with texture, mine came out very smooth. I would think any grainy or chunky issues would be from the heating process and suggest, as other reviewers have, that you mix all ingredients together before the slow heating process and stir continuously while heating. This will ensure a very smooth consistency. The pie is richer than a normal pudding

I've made this no-fail, always delicious pie many times since it originally appeared around 2001. Now, due to my granddaughter's celiac disease, I had the need to modify it in order to make it gluten free. Guess what? Even better! I used a "King Arthur Flour" gluten-free (rice flour & potato starch) pie crust from Walmart (my second use of this incredible tasty, flaky pie crust) and used CORN STARCH instead of flour in the pie filling (use a little more than half as much corn starch as flour -- a heaping 1/8 cup corn starch total). The pie was just a tad wobbly when I took it out of the oven and cooled to perfection. Another important modification that guarantees perfect results: mix your ingredients in a mixing bowl and just-melt the butter in the microwave before adding it into the mix (watch it and remove from heat before it is all melted and stir-melt the rest so that it is NOT piping hot) then slowly add it into the mix so as not to cook the egg in the mixture). THEN pour it into the crust and bake. Mine cook 45 minutes to perfection, and in an oven where "center of oven" for me (the position most recipes recommend fr everything) was a tad higher than center. I loved the rave reviews the recipe garnered - from non-celiac guests as well!

This pie is quite lovely! It's a rich, deep chocolaty flavor, and the meringue topping adds just the right amount of sweetness. I think I would tweak a couple things next time--like bake the filling and meringue both a bit longer; and I would leave the pie to cool in the oven after shutting it off. My meringue shrank back from the edges of the pie; and I believe that's from cooling too quickly. So I would try letting it cool more slowly next time to see if that makes a difference. I also pressed my filling through a fine mesh strainer before adding to the pie crust; and I really recommend doing that. It strained out all the lumps that might've formed, and kept the filling silky smooth. I'd like to try adding some heavy cream in place of the evaporated milk, and replace some of white sugar with brown to see if that will elevate the flavor a bit more. Otherwise, it came out really nice! Thank you for sharing your recipe!

Our grandmother died earlier this year and I needed a choc pie recipe since she was our choc pie maker. I had read reviews and some were negative and mostly those were saying that this is more like pudding or fudge. Here’s my opinion:the instructions didn’t mention anything about needing to let the pie cool before covering it to take somewhere. I needed to transport this pie and browned the meringue and after taking it from oven I immediately covered it and put in vehicle as I was pressed for time. I think I needed to let it cool back down before serving Bc the pie turned into liquid. But once I got it to where we were going and it cooled back off, it stiffened back up. 
 I made this into two pie shells rather than one deep dish. I prepared exactly as recipe called for only heating to melt the butter and poured equally into two gently prebaked shells. I baked for about 30 mins and removed and let cool completely. Then made the meringue. I used four egg white per pie. So I used 8 whites total. I spooned onto the pies and put back in oven on 350. Maybe here I should’ve put on broil or maybe used a torch. But it was after baking that the pies liquified again. 

They taste wonderful and I will keep this recipe as my go to choc pie recipe.

Loved this recipe for the pie. Only thing I changed was the recipe for the meringue, in which I added 1-1/2 teaspoon of cream of tartar in with the egg whites and mixed until foaming. I then gradually added 3/8 (1/4 cup + roughly half of 1/4 cup) cups of sugar while using an electric mixer for about 10-15 minutes.

This pie is great! I made it pretty much by the recipe, with just a few changes. I mixed everything in my saucepan (adding an extra tbsp of cocoa) and cooked it on the stove until it starting boiling. (about 5-8 min) Poured it in the crust and baked it for exactly 40 min. I also tented my crust edges with foil so it wouldnt brown too much. It came out perfect. It still had a little wobble to it, but it firmed up as it sat. I used a tried and true meringue recipe (3 egg whites, 1/4 tsp cream of tarter, and 6 tbsp sugar) it took about 15 min to brown. It truely is a different consistency than a typical chocolate pie and it is really sweet, but we all thought it was great. (Even my mom who isnt a chocolate pie lover :)

I followed one reviewers suggestion and reduced the sugar teo 1.5 cups. It was still way to sweet for us (and we like sweet). What I will say that I will definately make this again with less sugar (1 cup). It did not get runny, it was a perfect consistancy and a good chocolate flavor. I have never made a meringue pie before. My mother in law brings one every Thanksgiving and bless her heart it is always runny. So when mine came out so good I was really surprised. I owe it to the recipe. One trick I read about is make sure you put the meringue on the hot pie (this helps cook the bottom of the meringue even before it hits the oven) and seal the pie edges with the meringue (the meringue needs to touch the edges of the crust) or it will weep (little beads of syrup come through the meringue when it is done baking and cooling due to moisture getting in from the exposed pudding). Thanks for posting!!! I just may make the chocolate pie next Thanksgiving~!

Love this pie. Been looking for this recipe for a while. I added extra vanilla to. And I put the meringue on when the pie was almost done so the middle was still slightly wobbly. Baked an extra 13 minutes and there you go. Oh and for a deeper chocolate flavor an extra tbsp or two of chocolate. Yummy so good

I made this tonight. I would like to thank Stephanie for her suggestion to use 1 1/2 cup sugar and to blend everything together in the blender. I also added 1/2 tsp salt to the mixture. It was super easy. The texture of the pie was similar to pumpkin pie.

I only used 1 cup of sugar and did heaping tablespoons of cocoa. I also followed the recipe and didn't heat until everything was in the mixture. The meringue took about 12 minutes to brown. The texture was thicker than I thought it would be but was delicious. My nephews gave it 5 stars.
I’ve made this recipe for years it’s so amazing & delicious, my family always asks me to make it.
Only chocolate pie I’ve made for years all my neighbors have got this recipe for me
Excellent pie, well worth the effort. Will make it again - soon!

Absolutely the richest chocolate pie I’ve ever made. My husband LOVED it. I followed the recipe exactly, EXCEPT I had to bake it an extra 15 minutes. Then I immediately topped it with meringue and baked another ten minutes. After cooling I put it in the fridge overnight! It was so good.
Simple pie for beginners, always my go to.

Easy to make. I used a homemade crust, which I prefer. A really nice pie. I topped mine with homemade whipped cream after the pie had been completely cooled overnight in the refrigerator. Another thing I like is the low cost.

This recipe is phenomenal!! I did make a few adjustments. I added a tsp of kosher salt to the dry mixture, and I add my vanilla after the bitterness is melted and pan removed from heat. The vanilla flavor, along with the smooth, creamy chocolate just compliments it even more when the flavor is full. This recipe is my husband’s favorite, even over homemade NY Cheesecake, and it is always a family favorite! Unlike all the other chocolate pie recipes on here, for sure!

This just came out of the oven...for the 2nd time. My filling did set in the specified time, however after about 10 minutes, my meringue looked great, but was still very soft, which I realized after an hour of cooling. I reheated the oven and stuck it back in for 4 or 5 minutes, and the meringue outside firmed up nicely, while everything below it stayed soft. I am very excited for it, and I believe this was the way to go for a soft center.
Wonderful! Family asks for this every time!
